overview:
This is the route most travellers dream of when they think of Morocco: leave Marrakech, cross the High Atlas, follow the road of a thousand kasbahs to the edge of the Sahara, sleep among the dunes of Erg Chebbi, then drive north through cedar forests to Fes. Instead of returning to your starting point, you finish in a new city, which saves you a long day of driving back.

What makes this version different is the third day. Instead of rushing out of the desert the morning after your camel trek, you stay a full day around Merzouga – time for the Gnawa musicians of Khamlia, the nomad families, the fossil beds and a second desert sunset.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 4 days, 3 nights
• Start: Marrakech (hotel or riad pick-up) – Finish: Fes (drop-off at your accommodation)
• Total distance: about 1,100 km
• Nights: 1 Dades Valley guesthouse, 1 Sahara desert camp, 1 desert camp or Merzouga hotel (your choice)
• Type: private tour with driver in a 4x4 or minivan
• Activity level: easy to moderate (long drives, camel ride, short walks)

WHY THIS ITINERARY WORKS
The long drives are broken into stops every hour or two, the hardest leg (Merzouga to Fes) comes at the end, and the full day in Merzouga means you actually experience the desert rather than just sleep in it.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
First-time visitors who want both great cities and the Sahara, couples, families with children over six, and photographers.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you need to return to Marrakech, take the [4-day Marrakech to Merzouga tour](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/4-day-marrakech-to-merzouga-desert-adventure-including-2-nights-in-merzouga/685bc9fed3965e7948ffb7d3). With only three days, our [3-day Marrakech to Fes desert tour](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/marrakech-to-fes-3-day-desert-tour-via-merzouga/2475619d6a1ae949a8c3eb63) covers the same road with one desert night.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Pack layers: the Tichka pass and the desert at night can be cold, even in spring. Bring a small bag for the camp night; your main luggage stays in the vehicle. Cash for lunches, tips and optional activities is useful because cards are rarely accepted outside the cities.
descriptions:
The first day is the most scenic. You climb into the High Atlas, cross the Tizi n'Tichka pass, walk through Ait Ben Haddou and drive the Valley of the Roses to the Dades Valley, where you sleep in a guesthouse under the cliffs.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates and adapt to traffic and season)
07:30 – Pick-up at your hotel or riad in Marrakech.
09:00 – Coffee stop in the Atlas foothills near Taddert (about 20 min).
10:00 – Tizi n'Tichka pass, 2,260 m: photo stop (about 15 min).
11:30 – Ait Ben Haddou: guided walk through the ksar (about 1.5 hours).
13:00 – Lunch near Ait Ben Haddou (about 1 hour, not included).
14:30 – Ouarzazate: outside view of the Taourirt Kasbah (about 20 min).
15:30 – Skoura palm grove and kasbahs from the road.
16:30 – Kelaat M'Gouna, Valley of the Roses: short stop.
18:00 – Arrive at your guesthouse in the Dades Valley; dinner and overnight.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Tichka road has many hairpin bends. If you get car-sick, sit in front and take medication before leaving.
• Ait Ben Haddou is free to enter, but some houses charge a small fee to visit their rooms or roof.
• Rose products are sold everywhere in Kelaat M'Gouna; the harvest is in late April and May.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, fuel, guesthouse night with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, local guide at Ait Ben Haddou (optional), drinks, tips.

IF THE WEATHER TURNS: snow occasionally closes the Tichka pass in winter for a few hours. Your driver checks conditions early and waits or adjusts the timing if needed.

WHAT YOU'LL TASTE
Lunch near Ait Ben Haddou is usually a tagine or a set menu with salad and fruit. Dinner at the guesthouse is home cooking: harira soup, a chicken or vegetable tagine, couscous on some nights, and mint tea.

PHOTO SPOTS
• The view from the top of Ait Ben Haddou's granary over the river and the plain.
• The hairpin road below the Tichka pass.
• Kasbahs among the palm trees of Skoura.
• The Dades cliffs at golden hour from your guesthouse terrace.

ACCESSIBILITY
Ait Ben Haddou is on a hill with steep, uneven steps; you can enjoy the view from the river bank if climbing is hard. The rest of the day is mostly in the vehicle with short, easy stops.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: the change from the green Atlas to the red south, and your first sight of the kasbah country.

A shorter driving day ends with the highlight of the trip: a camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset and a night in a desert camp.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:00 – Breakfast at the guesthouse.
09:00 – Drive to Tinghir (about 1 hour), view over the palm grove.
10:15 – Todra Gorge: walk between the cliffs (about 1 hour).
11:30 – Short walk in the Tinghir palm grove or a carpet cooperative (optional, about 30 min).
12:30 – Lunch in Tinejdad or on the way (about 1 hour, not included).
14:30 – Erfoud: fossil workshop (about 30 min).
15:30 – Rissani or the road past the Merzouga oasis.
16:30 – Arrive at the edge of the Erg Chebbi; leave your main luggage in the vehicle.
17:00 – Camel trek into the dunes for sunset (about 1–1.5 hours).
18:30 – Arrive at the camp; mint tea.
20:00 – Dinner, drumming around the fire, stars.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The camel trek time follows the sunset, so it moves from about 16:00 in winter to about 18:30 in summer.
• Pack a small overnight bag: toothbrush, warm layer, head torch, any medicine.
• Camel rides are gentle but can be uncomfortable for people with back problems; a 4x4 transfer to camp is possible.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, camel trek with a camel handler, desert camp night with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

IF THE WEATHER TURNS: sandstorms happen, mostly in spring. If wind makes the camel trek unsafe, you go to camp by 4x4 and ride the camels when it calms down.

WHAT YOU'LL TASTE
At camp: soup, salads, tagine and fruit, sometimes madfouna – the 'Berber pizza' of the region, a flatbread stuffed with spiced meat and onions and baked in the sand or an oven.

PHOTO SPOTS
• The narrowest part of the Todra Gorge with its 300-metre walls.
• The Tinghir palm grove from the viewpoint above the town.
• Camel shadows on the dunes at sunset.
• The Milky Way above the camp on a moonless night.

ACCESSIBILITY
The Todra walk is flat along the riverbed. Dunes are soft and tiring to climb; the camp itself is on fairly flat sand. Tell us in advance if you need the 4x4 option.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: silence, sand, stars – the moment everyone remembers.

Wake before dawn to watch the sun rise over the dunes, then spend the whole day discovering the Merzouga region at an easy pace. In the evening you choose between a second night in the camp or a hotel at the foot of the dunes.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates and follow sunrise)
06:00 – Climb a dune near camp for sunrise (about 45 min).
07:00 – Camel ride back to the edge of the dunes.
08:00 – Breakfast and shower at a hotel or the camp.
10:00 – 4x4 tour around the Erg Chebbi (optional, about 4 hours): nomad family, Khamlia, old mines.
10:30 – Visit a nomad family and share tea in their tent (about 45 min).
11:45 – Khamlia: Gnawa music and the story of the village (about 45 min).
13:00 – Lunch in Merzouga (about 1 hour, not included).
14:00 – Rest by the pool or in the shade during the hottest hours.
16:30 – Sandboarding or a walk on the dunes (optional).
18:00 – Sunset from a high dune.
20:00 – Dinner and overnight at the camp or the hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• This day is flexible: tell your driver whether you want to be active or rest.
• The 4x4 tour, sandboarding and quad biking are extras, paid locally or on booking.
• In summer the middle of the day is very hot; activities happen in the morning and late afternoon.

INCLUDED: private driver for the day, accommodation (camp or hotel) with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, optional 4x4 tour, quad biking, sandboarding, tips.

IF THE WEATHER TURNS: on windy days, the music in Khamlia and the nomad visit go ahead, and the dunes wait for the evening.

WHAT YOU'LL TASTE
Mint tea with a nomad family, poured from high to create foam. In Merzouga, try a fresh madfouna or a kalia, a spiced stew of minced meat, tomatoes and eggs.

PHOTO SPOTS
• Sunrise on the eastern crests of the Erg Chebbi.
• The colourful costumes and drums of the Gnawa musicians in Khamlia.
• The dark stony plain (hamada) against the orange dunes.

ACCESSIBILITY
Most of the day can be done by vehicle with short walks. Climbing dunes is hard work; your driver will pick easy viewpoints if needed.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: real time in the desert, not just one night – and the people who live there.

The longest drive of the trip, but a beautiful one: from the dunes through the date palms of the Ziz valley, over the Middle Atlas and through the cedar forests, to arrive in Fes in the evening.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
07:30 – Breakfast; depart Merzouga.
08:15 – Rissani and Erfoud from the road.
09:30 – Ziz Valley viewpoint over the palm grove (about 15 min).
10:30 – Errachidia; coffee stop.
11:30 – Ziz Gorges and the Hassan Addakhil dam lake.
13:00 – Lunch in Midelt (about 1 hour, not included).
15:00 – Cedar forest near Azrou: Barbary macaques (about 20 min).
15:45 – Ifrane: short walk (about 30 min).
17:30–18:00 – Arrive in Fes; drop-off at your riad or hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The drive is about 470 km. It is long, but the scenery changes all day.
• Please do not feed the monkeys; it harms them.
• If you are flying out of Fes, book flights for the next day.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, drop-off in Fes.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

IF THE WEATHER TURNS: in winter the Middle Atlas can have snow and fog. Your driver adapts the route and timing.

WHAT YOU'LL TASTE
Midelt is known for its apples and its grilled meat restaurants. In Ifrane, try a coffee and a pastry in one of the cafés around the central square.

PHOTO SPOTS
• The endless palm groves of the Ziz valley from the roadside viewpoint.
• The blue lake of the Hassan Addakhil dam.
• Cedar trees and macaques near Azrou.
• The stone lion of Ifrane.

ACCESSIBILITY
Stops are short and close to the vehicle. Ifrane's town centre is flat with good pavements.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: the full width of Morocco in one day, from the Sahara to the cedar forests and the oldest imperial city.

faq.question: Does this tour return to Marrakech?
faq.answer: No. It starts in Marrakech and finishes in Fes. If you need to return to Marrakech, choose [our 4-day Marrakech to Merzouga round trip](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/4-day-marrakech-to-merzouga-desert-adventure-including-2-nights-in-merzouga/685bc9fed3965e7948ffb7d3).

faq.question: How many nights are in the desert?
faq.answer: One night in a Sahara camp is guaranteed. On the third night you choose: a second night in the camp or a hotel at the foot of the dunes with a pool.

faq.question: How long are the drives?
faq.answer: Day 1 about 7–8 hours with stops, day 2 about 5 hours, day 3 very little, and day 4 about 8–9 hours. We stop every 1.5–2 hours.

faq.question: What kind of vehicle is used?
faq.answer: A private air-conditioned 4x4 for small groups, or a minivan for larger groups. You never share with strangers.

faq.question: Do I have to ride a camel?
faq.answer: No. If you prefer, a 4x4 can take you to the camp. Camel rides are gentle and suitable for most people, including children.

faq.question: Are the desert camps comfortable?
faq.answer: Yes. Tents have real beds and blankets. Depending on the option you book, tents have private bathrooms with showers and toilets, or shared facilities.

faq.question: Which meals are included?
faq.answer: Dinner and breakfast every night. Lunches are not included so you can choose where and what to eat; your driver will suggest good places.

faq.question: What is the best time of year for this tour?
faq.answer: Spring (March–May) and autumn (September–November) are ideal. Summer is very hot in the desert; winter is sunny but nights are cold.

faq.question: Is this tour suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, for children who can manage some long drives. Families love the camel trek and the camp. Child seats are available on request.

faq.question: Can I customise the itinerary?
faq.answer: Yes. Because the tour is private, you can add a night, change hotels or add activities like the 4x4 tour. Ask us when booking.

faq.question: Can we do the tour in the other direction, from Fes to Marrakech?
faq.answer: Yes. The same route works in reverse: Fes, Ifrane and the Middle Atlas on Day 1, two desert days around Merzouga, then the Todra and Dades gorges and Ait Ben Haddou on the way to Marrakech. Tell us your direction when booking.

faq.question: Where exactly does the tour end in Fes?
faq.answer: At your riad or hotel in Fes, usually between 17:30 and 18:00. If your riad is inside the medina, the driver stops at the nearest gate and a porter carries your bags. We can also drop you at Fes airport or the train station, or continue to Chefchaouen the next day as a transfer.

faq.question: Is there electricity and Wi-Fi at the desert camp?
faq.answer: Most camps have electricity, often solar, for lights and phone charging. Wi-Fi is limited or absent, and mobile data can be weak among the dunes, so download maps and music before you arrive. The hotels in Merzouga and the Dades have Wi-Fi.
